主要内容: Procter & Gamble (PG) reported strong earnings in the third quarter of fiscal 2014, with a 5% year-over-year increase in earnings per share to $1.04. Revenue remained at $20.6 billion, though it was impacted by unfavorable foreign exchange rates. Organic sales grew 3%, driven by a 6% increase in the Fabric Care and Home Care segment and 2% gains in the Beauty and Baby, Feminine, and Family Care segments. The Grooming segment grew 1%, while Health Care remained flat. The company also repurchased $1.5 billion of its stock and returned $1.7 billion in dividends, with a 7% increase in its quarterly dividend. This marks the 58th consecutive year of dividend growth. Looking ahead, Procter & Gamble plans to sell its global Pet Care business, including brands like Iams and Eukanuba, to Mars. CEO A.G. Lafley emphasized that this move aligns with the company's strategy to focus on core businesses. In contrast, Church & Dwight is expanding its global footprint through acquisitions. Church & Dwight's international business accounted for 17% of its total sales in 2013, up significantly from 2% in 2001. While Procter & Gamble generated $84.2 billion in revenue in 2013, Church & Dwight generated $3.2 billion. Analysts expect Church & Dwight to grow faster than Procter & Gamble, with projected revenue growth of 3.2% and EPS growth of 9% in fiscal 2014, compared to Procter & Gamble's projected growth of 1% and 4.2%, respectively. Both companies are considered solid investments in the consumer goods space, suitable for low-risk, long-term growth portfolios. Securities explicitly mentioned in the source include Church & Dwight (CHD).
